headline.text: Make the UAE the world's best in the Global Food Security Index by 2051
headline.quote: make the UAE the world's best in the Global Food Security Index by 2051
headline.analystNote: The latest Global Food Security Index edition found is 2022. In March 2026 Economist Impact published a different index, the Resilient Food Systems Index (60 countries); no UAE result was found. The headline target therefore has no current scoreboard. This tracker shows the same four dimensions from official FAO data as an independent proxy, not as the index itself.

analystSources.label: Global Food Security Index, editions to 2022

structure.text: A national food basket of 18 main types of food
structure.analystNote: The 18 items are not listed on the portal. Until the official list is available, the tracker uses a stand-in basket of major staples, labelled as such.

strategies.name: Ne'ma Food Loss and Waste Reduction Roadmap
strategies.level: Federal (Ne'ma, the National Food Loss and Waste Initiative, with the Ministry of Climate Change and Environment)

goals.text: Cut food loss and waste by 50% by 2030
goals.quote: cut food loss and waste by 50 per cent by 2030
goals.analystNote: No baseline is published. The national baseline study (about 3,000 participants across all seven emirates; household fieldwork in September 2025) was due to report in the first half of 2026; no published results were found as of 17 Nov 2026. Progress cannot be measured until the baseline is released.

strategies.name: Dubai Food Security Strategy
strategies.analystNote: Press reports from October 2026 describe an updated Dubai Food Security Strategy 2030 with numeric targets; those figures could not be confirmed on an official page and are not used.

goals.text: Build the emirate's preparedness to face crises
goals.quote: build the emirate's preparedness to face crises

signals.text: The Ministry of Climate Change and Environment is updating the National Food Security Strategy 2051 with the private sector, aiming for domestic production to meet 50% of the country's crop needs.

source.publisher: AGBI (press), via the monitored policy record

target.unit: % of crop needs from domestic production

signals.implication: When the updated strategy is published, the tracker must be re-baselined to its goals. A 50% crop target would give the local-production pillar its first numeric benchmark; how 'crop needs' is defined (with or without cereals) decides how far away it is.

signals.text: Dubai Food Security Strategy 2030 unveiled by the Dubai Environment and Climate Change Authority, aligned with the National Food Security Strategy 2051, with five pillars: food availability, affordability, quality and safety, sustainability and resilience, and industry empowerment.

source.publisher: WAM (state news agency), via the monitored policy record; not checked directly

signals.implication: The Dubai aims listed on the federal portal predate this update; the register will follow the 2030 strategy once its document is available.
